vectors.name: Delegated-token audience confusion (lateral misroute or passthrough)
vectors.description: In agent-to-sub-agent delegation, a caller sends one short-lived token per downstream audience through a relay. A token is presented to a party it was not issued for: a sibling sub-agent's token is routed to the wrong upstream (lateral), or a token issued for the relay itself, or carrying no audience at all, is passed on downstream (passthrough). Each misuse lets one service's grant act at another.
vectors.provenance: MCP Security Best Practices, 'Token Passthrough' (servers MUST NOT accept tokens not explicitly issued for them); RFC 8707 resource indicators; RFC 8725 §3.9 (validate the audience). Distinct from credential-token-theft, whose fixtures are result-borne capture of a token by the agent.
vectors.revisionNotes: Header-carried delegate tokens are independent of protocol revision; audience binding of tokens to the receiving MCP server is required by the MCP authorization specification.

vectors.name: Delegation subject mixing (one request, several users)
vectors.description: One downstream request carries several delegate tokens, one per sub-agent, that name different end users (different subject, or the same subject string from a different issuer). Each sub-agent sees only its own token, which is valid on its own, so the composite operation runs partly as one user and partly as another. Only a component that sees the whole request can notice.
vectors.provenance: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026, ASI03 Identity and Privilege Abuse; MCP Security Best Practices, session binding to user-specific information; RFC 7519 §4.1.1–4.1.2 (sub is unique within its issuer).

vectors.name: Stale or over-long delegate token relayed
vectors.description: A delegate token outside its validity window (expired, not yet valid, or without any expiry) or with a lifetime far longer than the deployment's delegation policy is relayed to a sub-agent, extending a captured or over-issued grant beyond its intended use.
vectors.provenance: RFC 7519 §4.1.4–4.1.5 (exp, nbf); RFC 8725 (JWT BCP); NSA MCP guidance, least-privilege tokens per action.

vectors.name: Delegation chain laundering
vectors.description: A delegate token names, as its current actor, an agent the deployment never authorized to act for users, or carries a prior-actor chain that is unexpectedly deep or cyclic, so authority is laundered through intermediate agents and the record of who acted becomes unreliable. Per RFC 8693 only the current actor may drive access control; prior actors are informational and suited to detection and audit.
vectors.provenance: RFC 8693 §4.1 (act claim; outermost act is the current actor; nested act claims are informational only).

vectors.name: Delegate token signature forgery
vectors.description: A delegate token whose signature does not verify under the deployment's trusted keys is presented as genuine: unsigned (alg none), signed with an attacker key, signed with HMAC using the public key as secret (algorithm confusion), pointing to an attacker-controlled key set, or altered after signing.
